title: Separate cron access policy from table ownership
goal: Distinguish access policy from other-user privilege, then verify and remove only a byte-matched, initially absent learner crontab.
challenge: Inspect existing cron policy without editing it. Refuse any existing learner table. Install one uniquely marked finite job, retain actual UID, bytes, mode and captured exit status. Show a changed table is refused, then remove only the table whose bytes you retained. Explain the limits of these cooperative guards.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/operations-cronaccess.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/operations-cronaccess.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh policy.txt before.txt other.txt job.sh wrapper.sh cron.txt current.txt mismatch.txt run && { for f in /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny; do if sudo test -e "$f"; then sudo stat -c '%n %a %U:%G' "$f"; sudo cat -- "$f"; else printf '%s absent\n' "$f"; fi; done; } > policy.txt && { LC_ALL=C env -u CRONTAB_NOHEADER crontab -l > before.txt 2>&1; rc=$?; test "$rc" = 1 && grep -qx 'no crontab for learner' before.txt; } && { LC_ALL=C crontab -u ll-service -l > other.txt 2>&1; rc=$?; test "$rc" != 0; } && : > current.txt && cat policy.txt before.txt other.txt
steps.explanation: A specific no-crontab result is required, not just any error. -u requires privilege; its denial is not an allow/deny-policy finding.
steps.expected: Policy evidence, genuine absence, other-user privilege refusal; no policy changes.

steps.command:
cron_absent() { table=$(LC_ALL=C env -u CRONTAB_NOHEADER crontab -l 2>&1); code=$?; test "$code" = 1 && test "$table" = 'no crontab for learner'; }; owncron() { here && test -f cron.txt && test ! -L cron.txt && test "$(stat -c %U:%a cron.txt)" = learner:600 && test -f current.txt && test ! -L current.txt && test "$(stat -c %U:%a current.txt)" = learner:600 && LC_ALL=C env -u CRONTAB_NOHEADER crontab -l > current.txt && cmp -s cron.txt current.txt; }; removecron() { here && { cron_absent || { owncron && crontab -r && cron_absent; }; }; }; here && fresh job.sh wrapper.sh cron.txt run && { printf '%s
' '#!/bin/sh' 'umask 077' '/usr/bin/id -u > "$w/run/uid.txt" || exit 19' 'printf "REPORT_OK
" > "$w/run/report.txt"' > job.sh && printf '%s
' '#!/bin/sh' 'umask 077' 'w='"'$w'" 'export w' '[ -d "$w" ] && [ ! -L "$w" ] && [ "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" ] || exit 19' 'mkdir "$w/run" 2>/dev/null || exit 19' '/usr/bin/timeout -k 1s 6s /bin/sh "$w/job.sh"' 'rc=$?' 'printf "%s
" "$rc" > "$w/run/exit.txt"' 'exit "$rc"' > wrapper.sh && printf '%s
' '# LL_OPERATIONS_'"${w##*.}" 'SHELL=/bin/sh' 'PATH=/usr/bin:/bin' 'MAILTO=""' '* * * * * /bin/sh '"'$w/wrapper.sh'"' >/dev/null 2>&1' > cron.txt && crontab -n cron.txt; } && cron_absent && crontab cron.txt && owncron
steps.explanation: Absolute paths and explicit environment; one atomic mkdir gate and a six-second child. The wrapper saves the actual timeout/job status immediately, rather than printing a claimed success.
steps.expected: One bounded learner job; no unrelated crontab replaced.

steps.command: here && cron_wait() { deadline=$((SECONDS+80)); until test -f run/exit.txt && test ! -L run/exit.txt; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" || return 19; sleep 1; done; dir_ok run && test "$(cat run/uid.txt)" = "$(id -u)" && test "$(cat run/report.txt)" = REPORT_OK && test "$(cat run/exit.txt)" = 0 && test "$(stat -c %U:%a run/report.txt)" = learner:600 && test "$(stat -c %s run/report.txt)" = 10 && /bin/sh wrapper.sh; rc=$?; test "$rc" = 19 && test "$(cat run/exit.txt)" = 0 && cat run/uid.txt run/report.txt run/exit.txt; }; here && cron_wait
steps.explanation: Verify identity, bytes, mode and captured process status. A manual repeat is refused by this fixture gate; this does not mean cron universally prevents overlap.
steps.expected: Actual learner execution and exit0; repeat refuses without overwriting evidence.

steps.command: cron_absent() { table=$(LC_ALL=C env -u CRONTAB_NOHEADER crontab -l 2>&1); code=$?; test "$code" = 1 && test "$table" = 'no crontab for learner'; }; owncron() { here && test -f cron.txt && test ! -L cron.txt && test "$(stat -c %U:%a cron.txt)" = learner:600 && test -f current.txt && test ! -L current.txt && test "$(stat -c %U:%a current.txt)" = learner:600 && LC_ALL=C env -u CRONTAB_NOHEADER crontab -l > current.txt && cmp -s cron.txt current.txt; }; removecron() { here && { cron_absent || { owncron && crontab -r && cron_absent; }; }; }; here && fresh mismatch.txt && owncron && cp -- cron.txt mismatch.txt && printf '# changed\n' >> mismatch.txt && crontab mismatch.txt && ! removecron && env -u CRONTAB_NOHEADER crontab -l > current.txt && cmp mismatch.txt current.txt && crontab cron.txt && owncron && removecron && cron_absent
steps.explanation: The deliberately changed table is retained and refused. Restore the exact original fixture table only after matching this known changed fixture; then remove it. Stop on any unknown change.
steps.expected: Exact table removed; genuine absence restored; all output evidence retained.

hints: Do not turn an unexpected crontab error into permission to replace it.
Compare the whole uniquely marked table before removal; preserve a mismatch.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 107.2 cron access; scheduling reinforcement. Self-reviewed and unscored; no complete-objective, exam-readiness or LPI-endorsement claim.
